cohort: The study analyzed prescription data from 41,885 pregnant and postpartum women using LMWH to manage venous thromboembolism (VTE).
finding: From 2016 to 2021, both the number of prescriptions and total costs for LMWH to manage VTE in pregnant and postpartum women increased, with advanced age, cesarean section, diabetes, miscarriage, and preterm birth identified as common VTE risk factors linked to LMWH prescription.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was identified as one of the most common pregnancy-related VTE risk factors linked to LMWH prescription, accounting for 25.60% of cases.
